 Good News for Norway: Haaland and Ødegaard Return to Training
 Erling Haaland and Martin Ødegaard have returned to training with Norway after raising concerns over minor physical issues. Ståle Solbakken welcomes back his two biggest stars ahead of the UEFA Nations League clash against Wales.
 Haaland and Ødegaard Ease Norway's Injury Concerns
 The concern lasted just one day in Norway's training camp. After a session marked by the absence of their two biggest stars, the Scandinavian side received encouraging news ahead of their final international fixtures of the year.
 Erling Haaland and Martin Ødegaard took part in Wednesday's training session at Ullevaal Stadium in Oslo after sitting out Tuesday's workout.
 Their absence had raised uncertainty, particularly given the importance of the upcoming UEFA Nations League matches.
 However, head coach Ståle Solbakken had attempted to ease concerns from the beginning, explaining that both players were dealing with minor issues and that the coaching staff had designed individual recovery programs.
 The return of Haaland , the Manchester City striker, and Ødegaard , the Arsenal captain, comes as a major relief for a team that needs its most influential players during a decisive week.
 Although it remains unclear whether both will be fit enough to play the full 90 minutes, their presence in training has significantly reduced concerns surrounding the national team.
 Solbakken Welcomes Players Back but Loses Strand Larsen
 The physical condition of the squad had become one of Solbakken's biggest concerns.
 During the first training session, between six and seven players were unable to participate fully in the exercises on the pitch, forcing the coaching staff to adjust their preparations.
 The manager explained that he expected 21 or 22 of the 23 players called up to be available, although he acknowledged that there were doubts surrounding some members of the squad.
 One of the main concerns involved Jørgen Strand Larsen , the Crystal Palace striker, who had been struggling with an ankle problem.
 The forward was ultimately ruled out of the international camp and replaced by Erik Botheim , who plays for Viking .
 The good news for Norway is that the rest of the squad was able to take part in Wednesday's session, including players such as Antonio Nusa and the two biggest names of the day, Haaland and Ødegaard .
 Having both players back is particularly important for maintaining the team's attacking balance. While Haaland provides its greatest goal-scoring threat, Ødegaard is responsible for dictating the tempo and connecting midfield with the forwards.

 Two Matches That Will Shape Norway's Future
 The Norwegian national team heads into its final two UEFA Nations League group-stage fixtures knowing that every point will matter.
 The first match will be against Wales on Saturday, November 14, at Ullevaal Stadium in Oslo.
 Three days later, on Tuesday, November 17, Norway will travel to face Denmark at Parken Stadium in Copenhagen.
 Solbakken's side enters this doubleheader under pressure to improve its position in the group and avoid complications in the standings.
 In addition to getting his biggest stars back, the head coach still has another important decision to make: who will start in goal.
 Ørjan Nyland and Egil Selvik are competing for a place in the starting lineup, although Solbakken has preferred to keep his decision private.
 The manager confirmed that he has a plan in place alongside goalkeeping coach Frode Grodås , but refused to reveal who will be between the posts against Wales .
 For now, the biggest news is that Norway once again has its two most influential players available in training.
 After a day of uncertainty, Haaland and Ødegaard are back on the pitch. And for a national team facing two crucial matches in just four days, few developments could have been more important.
 Key Takeaways From Haaland and Ødegaard's Return
 Erling Haaland and Martin Ødegaard returned to Norway's training sessions after missing Tuesday's workout due to minor physical issues.
 Jørgen Strand Larsen was ruled out of the international camp with an ankle problem and replaced by Erik Botheim .
 Norway will face Wales on November 14 and Denmark on November 17 in its final UEFA Nations League group-stage fixtures.
